title: Access to applications and data
summary: Who may get access to company applications, cloud projects and data, how it is given and taken away, and how often it is checked.
scope: Every internal application, cloud project and dataset. Customer accounts in our products are out of scope.

requirements.title: Access through groups only
requirements.statement: Access is given to access groups, never to a named person directly. People get access by joining a group through an approved request.
requirements.rationale: Access given to a person is invisible in reviews and stays when the person changes job.
guidance: Create one group per application and role, e.g. app-billing-readers.
Ask for membership with the process 'Request access to an application'.

verification.description: Code review of IAM changes and a monthly report of direct grants.

lookFor: An IAM binding with a member of the form user:name@example.com
A role granted to a personal account in Terraform or a manifest

requirements.title: Single sign-on for every application
requirements.statement: Internal applications let people sign in only with their company account through single sign-on; local user names and passwords are switched off.
requirements.rationale: When someone leaves, one switch removes all their access. Local accounts are forgotten.
guidance: Register the application in Entra ID.
Turn off local sign-in after the first admin has signed in through single sign-on.

verification.description: Checked when the application is registered and in the yearly audit.

requirements.title: No standing admin access in production
requirements.statement: Nobody has permanent owner or admin rights on production projects. Changes go through the pipeline; in an emergency, access is given for at most four hours with a second person's approval.
requirements.rationale: Standing admin access is the first thing an attacker with a stolen laptop looks for.
guidance: Remove owner and editor roles from people and groups on production projects.
Use the process 'Get emergency access to a production GCP project' when the pipeline cannot help.

verification.description: Daily policy check on all production projects.

lookFor: roles/owner or roles/editor granted on a production project
A group with admin rights added to a production subscription

requirements.title: Review access every six months
requirements.statement: The owner of a critical application confirms every six months that each member of its access groups still needs the access.
requirements.rationale: People change jobs more often than anyone asks to remove their access.
guidance: Answer the access review task that arrives in ServiceNow.
Remove everyone you do not recognise.

requirements.title: Read access by default
requirements.statement: Groups give the smallest role that does the job; read-only is the default and write access is a separate group.
requirements.rationale: Most people only need to look. Separate groups make write access visible in reviews.
guidance: Create a -readers and an -editors group for every application.
Use predefined roles; avoid custom roles with wildcards.

lookFor: A single group with both read and write roles
A custom role with permissions ending in .*
